transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I don’t care about the projects and hobbies I used to love anymore; nothing feels interesting to me now. I used to get so excited about tinkering with solar setups, painting, or going hiking, but lately, I just can't find the spark for any of it.
Have you felt this way for most days over the last two years, or is this a more recent change that has lasted for several weeks?

It’s been going on for a little over a year now. It really started when I lost a big solar contract for my side business and the financial pressure started getting tight. Since then, I've felt like this almost every single day.
Have you experienced any similar periods of feeling this low or losing interest in things before this past year, or has this been your first time feeling this way?
No, I've never really felt this way before. This past year is the first time I've ever experienced anything like this.
To clarify, have you experienced any other distinct periods of depression in your life, even if they were many years ago, or has this been your only episode?
No, this is definitely the first and only time I've ever felt like this. I've never experienced another period of depression or anything similar in my life before this past year.
Have you been able to continue working or managing your daily household responsibilities, or have your symptoms made it nearly impossible for you to function at work or at home?

It has been extremely difficult to keep up with everything. At work, I've started missing bid deadlines and turning in my repair reports late, which has really hurt my income. At home, I mostly just go straight to my couch to sit alone, so chores and bills are piling up while I cancel on my friends.
Beyond the loss of interest, have you experienced other symptoms like significant changes in your sleep, appetite, or feelings of worthlessness nearly every day?

Yes, I lie awake for hours worrying about bills and wake up exhausted at 3 AM, and food tastes like cardboard so I have to force myself to eat. I also feel like a complete screwup who doesn't deserve to own a home or have nice things because I let my business stall. It's like I'm constantly carrying this heavy guilt and exhaustion.

Do you feel that you have reached a point where you are completely unable to function or interact with others, or are you still able to manage a few essential tasks despite the overwhelming feelings of worthlessness and exhaustion?

I'm not completely unable to function because I still manage to drag myself to my main repair job, but I am barely getting by. I've been turning in my work reports late, missing bid deadlines, and letting my chores and bills pile up at home. Mostly, I just go straight home after my shifts to sit alone and end up canceling on my friends.
When you are at your worst, do you feel physically slowed down, like your movements and speech are labored, or do you feel a sense of restless agitation that makes it impossible to sit still?

I actually feel both of those things at the same time. Physically, I feel like I'm wading through mud and my coworkers even joke that I'm in slow motion, but on the inside, I have this restless, buzzing tension like I want to crawl out of my own skin.

Would you say that your inability to function is so severe that you are unable to perform even basic daily tasks, or are you still able to maintain some level of routine despite the significant impairment you described?

I'm still barely managing to go to work, though I'm slipping up, turning in reports late, and moving really slowly. Outside of work, my routine has completely collapsed—I just go straight home to sit alone, letting bills and chores pile up, and I even have to force myself to do basic things like eating.
